title: Reasoning traces, answer extraction and verifiable rewards
description: Chain of thought as inference compute; extracting a boxed answer, normalising notation and checking equivalence to get a deterministic right-or-wrong signal.

title: pass@k and error bars for evaluation
description: The unbiased pass@k estimator, why the plug-in version is biased, and standard errors and Wilson intervals for benchmark accuracy.

title: Inference-time scaling: voting, best-of-n and budgets
description: Temperature and top-p sampling, self-consistency (plurality voting), best-of-n with a scorer, token budgets, and the compute-accuracy trade-off under a binomial model.

title: Self-refinement, log-probability scoring and stopping rules
description: Scoring answers with heuristics and average log-probabilities, critique-and-revise loops, acceptance rules and when to stop refining.

title: GRPO: group-relative advantages and the clipped, KL-regularised objective
description: Policy gradient from verifiable rewards, group-relative advantages without a value network, the sequence-level loss, ratio clipping and the KL penalty, with a gradient check.

title: Reward design for verifiable reasoning tasks
description: Correctness and format rewards, conditional format rewards, zero-signal groups and monitoring reward and advantage statistics.

title: Improving GRPO: normalisation, clipping and monitoring
description: Length and standard-deviation normalisation effects, token-level versus sequence-level losses, asymmetric clipping, dynamic filtering, and entropy and advantage monitoring.

title: Distilling reasoning traces into small models
description: Hard and soft distillation, building SFT examples from teacher traces, verifier and length filtering, the answer-only cross-entropy loss.

title: Batching, padding and throughput for reasoning workloads
description: Latency versus throughput, left padding and attention masks, padding waste, and what batching does to evaluation, sampling, RL rollouts and distillation.
